## Punta Centinela: A Beach Holiday on Ecuador's Pacific Coast

Punta Centinela is a coastal area of Santa Elena Province on mainland [Ecuador](/ecuador/). Travelers come for the sandy beach, Pacific Ocean views and a few relaxing days after an active sightseeing itinerary. Unlike the Andean highlands and nature excursions to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), a typical day here may simply involve swimming, walking along the shore and resting.

The name appears both in descriptions of the coastline and in the name of the Royal Decameron Punta Centinela hotel complex. **The beach destination and a particular hotel are different things.** Visiting the area does not mean staying at that hotel or receiving all the services included in its packages.

## What the Coastline Looks Like

Punta Centinela's sandy shore faces the Pacific Ocean. Depending on the weather, waves may be gentle or quite powerful, so choose swimming areas according to current conditions and lifeguard advice. On a clear day, it is pleasant to walk along the surf, look at rocky stretches of coastline and watch the ocean.

For a beach holiday, the wind, currents and wave height matter just as much as air temperature. Even if photographs show calm water, sea conditions change daily. When traveling with children, choose sheltered sections and officially supervised swimming areas.

## Royal Decameron Punta Centinela: What to Know

**Royal Decameron Punta Centinela** operates in the area and describes its offering as all inclusive on its official website. The property has rooms, restaurants, pools and leisure facilities. It is located in Santa Elena Province and offers different types of accommodation.

Check the actual rate carefully. Even within one hotel, room categories, transfer arrangements, meal inclusions and available activities may differ. For example, excursions beyond the property, spa services and certain water activities may cost extra. Do not assume they form part of an Ada Tours package simply because the hotel offers them.

When selecting accommodation, decide whether you want to relax only at the resort, visit nearby coastal settlements or spend a certain number of days on the beach after flights.

## Getting Here from Guayaquil

The principal transport hub for mainland coastal journeys is [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/), with a road connecting it to Santa Elena. Royal Decameron's official website estimates approximately **2 hours of travel** from Guayaquil's international airport to the resort area. Actual journey time depends on traffic, the departure point and stops.

If the beach portion follows a trip to the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), coordinate the return flight to the mainland with ground transportation. Do not assume an international or domestic ticket automatically includes the drive to the hotel. Each transfer should be stated in the itinerary.

## Whale Watching and Marine Activities

Humpback whales can be observed off Ecuador's coast during their migration season. For the Santa Elena area, **June–October** is commonly mentioned as the period when whale-watching boat trips are organized. Sightings depend on the animals, while boat departures depend on forecasts and operators' schedules.

Whale watching requires a separately arranged excursion. A stay at Punta Centinela does not necessarily include a whale-watching trip. Likewise, snorkeling, diving, fishing and other boat outings have their own safety, equipment and payment conditions.

If ocean wildlife is your principal interest, allocate enough time to have an alternative plan in case a boat trip is canceled.

## Combining the Beach with a Journey Across Ecuador

Punta Centinela makes a relaxing finale to a route through Quito, the Andes or the Galápagos. Instead of changing hotels daily, stay several nights in one place. This can be particularly welcome after early departures, boat excursions and flights.

On the [Ada Tours “Ecuador, Galápagos and Humpback Whales” itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/), Punta Centinela forms part of the mainland coastal and beach section. Check hotel arrangements, all-inclusive services and marine excursions against that tour's own program, rather than a promotional list of all the area's possibilities.

Compare more journeys in the [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/) and the [beach holiday](/interests/beach-holidays/) section.

## When to Go and What to Bring

The coastal climate is different from high-altitude Quito. Bring lightweight clothing, sun protection, a hat and suitable beach footwear. During whale-watching season, it is helpful to arrange a marine excursion in advance; for a regular beach holiday, the main considerations are the weather and how long you want to stay.

If you find heat difficult, plan shoreline walks in the morning or toward evening. Remember the strong equatorial sun even on cloudy days and observe swimming restrictions.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Punta Centinela

### Is Punta Centinela on the Galápagos Islands?

No. It is on Ecuador's mainland Pacific coast, in Santa Elena Province. To combine it with the Galápagos, you need a flight to the mainland and an onward transfer.

### Is there an all-inclusive hotel here?

Yes. Royal Decameron Punta Centinela operates in the area. Exact inclusions depend on your accommodation package.

### Can I see humpback whales?

It is possible during the season, usually June to October, on a separate boat outing. Sightings cannot be guaranteed.

### How many days should I spend at the beach?

After a busy sightseeing journey, several nights without daily transfers are often more relaxing. The duration depends on whether you want beach time alone or additional marine excursions.

## Tours to Punta Centinela: Ocean, Beaches and Humpback Whales

[Punta Centinela](/ecuador/place/punta-centinela/) lies on Ecuador's Pacific coast on the Santa Elena Peninsula. It is a convenient place to finish a sightseeing journey with a few days by the sea after the highlands and the Galápagos nature routes. At certain times of year, the coastline is also a departure point for humpback whale-watching excursions.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Punta Centinela on the main route. The [“Ecuador, Galápagos and Humpback Whales” itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) runs on **August 11–21, 2027**. This is an 11-day, 10-night group departure for up to 15 participants, with the final three nights allocated to the coast.

## From the Andes to the Ocean

At the start of the journey, you explore [Quito and the Cotopaxi area](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). The itinerary then continues to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) before returning to the mainland.

On day 8, **August 18, 2027**, a flight is scheduled from [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) airport to [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/). From there, participants travel to the coast by road; the itinerary estimates approximately **2.5 hours** for the transfer. The remaining time is free.

Accommodation is planned for three nights at **Decameron Punta Centinela, all inclusive**. It is important to distinguish the hotel's meal and service system from the whole journey: all-inclusive arrangements during the beach stay do not mean the same basis applies in the Galápagos or highland cities.

## Why August Is Suitable for Whale Watching

Ecuador's Ministry of Tourism describes the annual humpback whale-watching season off the country's coast as running **from June to September**. The tour's August dates fall within this seasonal window. Even in season, however, whale appearances cannot be guaranteed at a particular time.

An ocean outing from the hotel area is scheduled for **August 20, 2027**. The current program allocates **45 minutes to 1 hour** for watching whales. The boat outing itself depends on weather and sea conditions. The group returns to the hotel afterward.

During whale watching, keep a safe distance, do not ask the captain to approach animals for photographs and follow the crew's instructions. Transfer duration, boarding, whether a departure can proceed and other exact arrangements are confirmed under the excursion's terms.

## A Beach Day Between the Flight and Boat Excursion

**August 19** is left free for relaxing by the Pacific Ocean. This makes the itinerary different from journeys scheduling another excursion immediately after a flight: travelers can rest before the whale-watching outing without changing hotels.

The journey therefore combines three different experiences: Andean mountain nature, island wildlife and the mainland coast. It suits travelers who want variety and are comfortable with several flights and significant changes in climate. Those whose priority is to maximize time in the Galápagos should compare [other Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) by their number of island days.

For the boat outing, bring wind-resistant clothing, sunscreen, nonslip shoes and protection against spray. Travelers prone to motion sickness should discuss the boat's characteristics ahead of time. Special equipment or services aboard must be confirmed separately.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Punta Centinela Tours

### Is Punta Centinela in the Galápagos?

No. It is on mainland Ecuador. Travelers fly from the Galápagos to Guayaquil, then continue to Punta Centinela by road.

### How many nights are planned on the coast?

The August 2027 itinerary includes **3 nights** at Decameron Punta Centinela on an all-inclusive basis.

### Is whale watching included in the journey?

A dedicated boat outing is scheduled for August 20. It depends on weather and sea conditions, and a sighting cannot be guaranteed.

### What time of year is best for a whale-watching trip?

The usual season off Ecuador's coast runs from June to September. Outside that window, check whether a similar excursion is offered in the specific itinerary.

## Punta Cormorant on Floreana: Green Sand and a Flamingo Lagoon

Punta Cormorant is located on [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Visitors arrive on authorized cruise routes to see unusual volcanic sands, a coastal lagoon and a beach where green sea turtles nest.

What makes the site particularly interesting is the combination of natural features that lie close together but look completely different. Visitors first land on a shore with a greenish tint to the sand, then follow a path beside the lagoon and reach a view of a pale beach on the other side. A short walk with a naturalist guide is usually sufficient to experience these landscapes.

The name can be misleading: **cormorants are not the main attraction at Punta Cormorant**. Flamingos and other waterbirds at the lagoon are its best-known wildlife sighting.

## Why Is the Sand Greenish?

The greenish color of the first beach comes from **olivine** crystals in the volcanic material. Such minerals occur in basaltic rocks in the Galápagos, and water and wind gradually break them down into sand and small fragments along the shore.

Do not expect a perfectly emerald beach in every kind of weather and light. Some areas show the color more clearly, while others are dominated by brown and dark volcanic tones. The contrast between the sand and the island's black rock is especially interesting.

On the other side of the trail lies a beach commonly called Flour Beach. Its very pale sand consists mainly of tiny coral fragments. Both shores form part of the same excursion stop, but their sand comes from different natural materials.

## The Flamingo Lagoon: What to Expect

A brackish lagoon lies between the beaches. Galápagos flamingos feed here, and visitors may also see ducks, stilts and other waterbirds. Flamingos move through shallow water, filtering food from the water and sediment.

The number of birds depends on season, water level and feeding conditions. **A lagoon does not guarantee a flock of flamingos every day.** The guide chooses observation points along the permitted trail so visitors can see the birds without approaching their resting or feeding areas.

A modest zoom lens or binoculars are helpful for photographs and observation: keeping your distance allows the birds to behave naturally. Walking slowly and quietly is more important than trying to approach the wildlife.

## Sea Turtle Nesting Beach: What Is Allowed?

The pale beach on the outer side of the point is a nesting ground for green sea turtles. During breeding season, tracks may be visible in the sand, and turtles or rays are sometimes seen near shore.

**Swimming is prohibited at Flour Beach.** Visitors view the shore only from authorized routes and follow the guide's instructions. Do not touch nests, tracks or eggs, or approach turtles.

| Feature | What makes it special |
|---|---|
| Greenish beach | Olivine mineral |
| Brackish lagoon | Flamingos and waterbirds |
| Pale beach | Sea turtle nesting site |

This compact walk introduces visitors to Floreana's volcanic geology, birdlife and marine ecology in one outing.

## What a Cruise Excursion Involves

A visit usually begins with the vessel approaching [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) by sea. Depending on anchoring conditions, passengers may travel ashore in small boats and make a wet landing on the beach. After the briefing, the group walks along an authorized path.

The island has other visitor sites, including [Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/), a marine volcanic feature where snorkeling is organized when currents are safe. This is **a separate stop**: a walk at Punta Cormorant is not the same as snorkeling among the rocks at Devil's Crown.

On the [Ada Tours 8-day VIP Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), you visit Punta Cormorant during the day on Floreana together with other island sites. The [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) schedules a separate walk to the point's lagoon. Check actual landing arrangements and possible water activities against your chosen itinerary.

## Seasons and Natural Conditions

Water temperatures, wind and rainfall change across the Galápagos seasons. Flamingos can be seen near the lagoon at different times of year, but their position and the likelihood of sightings vary. Green sea turtles nest on Floreana's beaches during the warmer part of the year; a normal daytime excursion should not be expected to include watching nighttime nesting.

The lagoon and beaches are protected under Galápagos National Park rules. Do not collect sand, stones, shells or plants, feed animals or leave permitted routes. For a short walk, bring footwear suitable for landings and sand, sun protection and drinking water.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Punta Cormorant

### Where is Punta Cormorant?

On Floreana Island in Ecuador's Galápagos archipelago. It is usually visited on an expedition cruise.

### Why does the beach look green?

Because of olivine crystals in the volcanic material. The sand's color depends on lighting and the composition of each area.

### Are flamingos always there?

The lagoon is known for flamingos, but their numbers and visibility change. A sighting is not guaranteed.

### Can you swim at the pale beach?

Restrictions apply at Flour Beach because sea turtles nest there. The visit is organized as a walk and a chance to observe wildlife, not free swimming.

## Punta Cormorant as a Possible Stop on a Diving Tour

[Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/) is on [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the Galápagos archipelago. It is best known for its greenish olivine sand, pale beach and brackish lagoon where flamingos sometimes feed.

Here we consider **tours with an optional visit**, rather than primary cruise routes through the point. Our catalog has {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} offering a possible visit to the point. It is important to distinguish walking ashore on Floreana from underwater diving in the island's waters.

## What the Diving Program Offers

The [4- or 5-day Galápagos diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) is based on Santa Cruz Island at Hotel Fiesta. After arriving on Baltra, participants visit the Santa Cruz highlands, meet the dive center staff and check equipment.

The 4-day option includes **2 days of diving**; the 5-day option includes **3**. Each day at sea provides two dives, with a surface interval, a snack and lunch. Trips depart in the morning and return to the base afterward. Exact dive sites are assigned according to ocean conditions, weekday and the group's experience.

Punta Cormorant is listed among possible sites alongside other areas of Galápagos waters. **Being named on the list does not guarantee that the boat will travel here.** Moreover, even a dive site selected near Floreana is not equivalent to landing at the flamingo lagoon: a shore visit and a dive are different activities.

## When to Choose a Cruise Instead of a Diving Tour

| Main goal | Suitable format |
|---|---|
| Lagoon and beaches | Cruise with a shore landing |
| A series of dives | Diving based on an island |

Travelers mainly interested in flamingos, the olivine shore and the walking trail should compare the [8-day VIP yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) and the [18-day Ecuador tour with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/). Both include Punta Cormorant in the main marine route around Floreana.

On the yacht cruise, it appears near the start of the island itinerary; on the longer tour, it follows the journey through mainland Ecuador. A closer comparison is available in the [Punta Cormorant tour catalog](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/tour/).

The diving program serves another purpose: it allows you to select **how much diving to do** while staying in one hotel. Do not assume that any specific shore landing is included without separate confirmation.

## Requirements for Divers

Under the current diving-tour description, the minimum age is 12. Certified diving requires PADI, NAUI, CMAS or an equivalent qualification. Separate introductory dives and training are offered to beginners without certification, subject to conditions agreed separately.

The tour describes included equipment, but some accessories and specialized cylinders cost extra. Medical requirements depend on health and how long it has been since the last dive. Before booking, inform the dive center of your experience, certification and significant contraindications, and agree on the interval between the last dive and your flight off the islands.

The Galápagos National Park authority regulates permitted sites and types of marine activity. This is another reason not to base a journey on the promise of one particular dive site before it has been confirmed.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Trips to Punta Cormorant

### Does a diving tour guarantee a stop at Punta Cormorant?

No. It is one of the potential sites. The dive center chooses the actual route based on weather, ocean conditions and participants' experience. The number of diving days and dives is specified by the selected program.

### Will I see the flamingo lagoon during a diving tour?

Visiting the lagoon requires an onshore itinerary on Floreana. Listing a dive site does not mean a landing or walk is included. For a land visit, see [cruises visiting the point](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/tour/).

### How do the 4- and 5-day options differ?

The main difference is **2 or 3 days of diving**, with respectively 3 or 4 nights at Fiesta. Both options involve the selection of actual dive sites, not a fixed stop at Punta Cormorant.

### Can I combine a cruise with additional dives?

That would require separate confirmation of schedules, flights, post-dive rest and service inclusions. It is not automatically part of this tour. The [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/) can help with choosing the overall geography.

## Tours to Punta Cormorant in the Galápagos Islands

[Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/) is located on [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the Galápagos archipelago. On one short walk, you can see a shore with greenish olivine sand, a brackish lagoon with flamingos and a paler beach made of fine coral fragments. The visit is usually part of an inter-island expedition cruise.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Punta Cormorant on the main itinerary. Choose based on **the full length of the journey, time at sea and nearby stops on Floreana**. The lagoon visit itself is relatively short, but the broader sea routes can be very different.

## Two Routes Visiting Punta Cormorant

| Program | Place in the itinerary |
|---|---|
| [8-day VIP Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) | Floreana, day 2 |
| [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos cruise journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) | Floreana, day 16 |

On the [8-day yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), the yacht reaches Floreana on the morning of day 2. After a wet landing, travelers walk to the lagoon at Punta Cormorant, where flamingos and other shorebirds may be seen. They then return aboard, with a choice of kayaking or traveling to [Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/) for snorkeling. In the afternoon, the itinerary continues to Post Office Bay and the Baroness viewpoint. This option focuses on the islands themselves and sea journeys between them.

On the [18-day journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), travelers first spend an extended period exploring mainland Ecuador: the Andes, cloud forests and Amazon. The Galápagos part lasts 4 days and 3 nights aboard a yacht. On day 16, after visiting Post Office Bay, the yacht continues to Punta Cormorant. A walk of approximately 2 km to the flamingo lagoon is scheduled, with a wet landing, an easy difficulty rating, snorkeling and a motorboat outing. Devil's Crown follows later, without a shore landing there.

**The main distinction:** the shorter yacht cruise is entirely about the islands, while on the 18-day tour Punta Cormorant is one of the final nature experiences on a much broader journey across mainland Ecuador.

## What to See at the Point and Nearby Bays

Punta Cormorant's most recognizable feature is the lagoon where flamingos feed in shallow water. Their numbers vary, so watching requires quiet and patience. Olivine crystals give the first beach its greenish tint, while the paler sand across the trail is made of fine coral fragments. Comparing two distinct natural environments so close together is a highlight.

The shore visit and snorkeling are different parts of the day. [Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/) is known for marine life around the remnants of a volcanic formation, but access to the water follows its own conditions. Do not assume every water activity listed for the Floreana marine itinerary takes place at Punta Cormorant.

For choosing islands, also compare [Galápagos routes in the Ecuador catalog](/ecuador/tour/) and [the country's nature and wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). Not every itinerary passing Floreana includes this point.

## Landing, Weather and Preparation

A **wet landing** means moving from a boat to shore through shallow water. Bring footwear suitable for wet sand and waterproof protection for your phone or camera. A hat, water and sunscreen are useful for the coastal path. Snorkeling depends on the selected tour, weather and sea conditions.

Island itineraries may change on crew instructions and under conservation rules. A particular encounter with a flamingo, turtle or ray cannot be guaranteed. Allow time to watch wildlife while keeping your distance.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Punta Cormorant Cruises

### Where is Punta Cormorant?

On Floreana Island in Ecuador's Galápagos archipelago. Sea itineraries connect it with other stops on Floreana and nearby islands.

### How do the two tours differ?

The [8-day cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) is devoted to the Galápagos. The [18-day tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) combines the Andes, Amazon and a four-day cruise, so island time is a smaller proportion of the whole journey.

### Can I see flamingos on any given day?

Flamingos do inhabit the lagoon, but their numbers and how close they can be observed vary. The visit promises an introduction to the place, not a guaranteed number of birds.
